The test image shows a sugarcane leaf with:
- A prominent white/cream stripe running along the midrib
- Green tissue on both sides
- A reddish-brown discoloration mark on the lower portion of the white stripe

This pattern strongly suggests **Leaf_Scald** (white midrib stripe + reddish discoloration). Let me verify with one reference image.

The Leaf_Scald reference shows a **horizontal white band** crossing the full width of the leaf — that does not match the test image, which shows a **vertical white stripe along the midrib** running the full length of the leaf.

The test image features:
- White/cream coloring concentrated along the central midrib (running lengthwise)
- Green tissue on both margins
- A small reddish-brown spot on the whitened midrib area

This pattern — midrib whitening/yellowing — is the hallmark of **Yellow_Leaf** disease ("yellowing specifically of the midribs"). The reddish spot could represent early necrosis consistent with that disease's progression.
